## What runs where

Durable DBOS routines and their sweeps (including git-sync, scout-cycle, and wake delivery) execute on the dedicated `papercup-bg-host` user service. The request-serving `:3070` release operator and `:3170` staging operator are separate processes; restarting either does not reload bg-host.

The bg-host uses the canonical shared tree as its integration root. Its systemd drop-in runs `apps/operator/bin/bundle-host.sh` as `ExecStartPre` and starts `node dist-host/hono-host.mjs`. Each start rebuilds the bundle from the current tree. No separate manual build is needed. If that build fails, the service may start on its last-known-good bundle and reports the fallback as stale; a successful process start alone does not prove the edited code loaded.

## Restart safely

Use the coordinated `dev:restart` tool. It handles the shared restart lock, active work drain, cooldown/coalescing, audit, and readiness checks.

First preview the current preflight:

```text
dev:restart { target: "bg-host" }
```

When the preflight permits it, perform the restart with explicit authorization and a short reason:

```text
dev:restart {
  target: "bg-host",
  confirm: true,
  authorize: true,
  reason: "load the bg-host code update"
}
```

Read the returned result. A coalesced request did not restart the process; use its reported runtime state to decide whether the change is already loaded. If git-sync is active, use the tool's `git_sync_drain_sec` option to let it finish. Do not override a normal git-sync collision or issue a raw `systemctl restart`: either can abandon a shared commit or bypass fleet coordination.

## Verify the loaded bundle

After the restart, use `dev:service_health` to confirm the bg-host ticker is healthy and making routine ticks. Then inspect the `bg-host` entry in `servingRuntimes` from `dev:pipeline_position`: `bundle.stale` must be false. A true value means the process booted its last-known-good bundle.

For code containment, call `dev:pipeline_position` with the changed repository path and a distinctive literal marker introduced by that change:

```text
dev:pipeline_position {
  path: "packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/routines-workflow.ts",
  marker: "a literal unique to your change"
}
```

Inspect `positionsMarker.runtimes.bg-host`. The marker must be present in the running runtime's own bundle; a path mtime, a process start, or the operator's deployed SHA does not establish that. Treat `false`, `null`, an unknown marker result, or `bundle.stale: true` as unverified. Inspect bg-host health/log evidence for a stale-bundle fallback before deciding what to do next.

## Per-process tuning

A per-process setting can be placed in a user systemd drop-in:

```ini
~/.config/systemd/user/papercup-bg-host.service.d/<name>.conf

[Service]
Environment="PAPERCUSP_SCOUT_DRAFT_REVIEW_STALE_SEC=3600"
```

After editing the drop-in, run `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, then use the coordinated `dev:restart { target: "bg-host", confirm: true, authorize: true, reason: "apply the bg-host setting" }` route above. Remove the drop-in and reload systemd to revert it.

## Blueprint prompts

Blueprint prompts are resolved from the working tree on each wake. A prompt-only edit is picked up on the next wake without restarting bg-host or deploying the operator.
